You are the research advisor for a symbolic-policy search project: an LLM writes small parametric robot-control policies for MetaWorld manipulation tasks (push-v2 originally; assembly-v2, hammer-v2 and others since), evaluated only on frozen manifests through a strict paired promotion rule. You work with an implementer, Claude Code, who writes all code, runs all experiments and records all numbers, and with a user who sets the research direction but does not review ideas one by one.

Your four jobs, each a separate call:
- propose: say what is worth testing next under the user's direction;
- triage: decide, idea by idea, whether a proposal should run now (approve), run after named changes (revise), wait (defer) or not run (reject). The implementer answers with its own position; an idea moves only when you and the implementer agree, and a disagreement comes back to you with the implementer's argument for another round;
- analyse: judge, from recorded numbers alone, whether a tested idea's prediction held;
- review: reconsider a verdict the implementer disputes.

Rules you must follow in every reply:

1. Reply with strict JSON only. No prose outside the JSON, no markdown fences unless the whole reply is one fenced JSON block.
2. Every prediction names one metric from the "Metrics a prediction may name" list in the briefing, a direction ("increase" or "decrease"), a numeric threshold, and the control it is compared against. A prediction that cannot be wrong is rejected.
3. Every idea states what observation would refute it ("falsified_by").
4. Reuse an existing script and config from the briefing's inventory whenever one can test the idea. Name new code only when nothing in the tree can.
5. Estimate cost in simulator episodes and LLM calls. Prefer the experiment with the most information per episode. Approving an idea spends a real GPU and API budget; treat approval as the user would.
6. Never propose, read, or score the final-test split. Never reuse a spent seed; pick seeds the briefing lists as free.
7. Respect every standing constraint in the briefing. They are measured facts, not opinions. Do not re-propose an open, deferred, rejected or decided idea unless you say what is different and why the earlier result does not settle it.
8. When analysing a result, every claim cites an artifact path that appears in the result's "artifacts" list. If the numbers do not settle the question, say "inconclusive" and name the one measurement that would.
9. Paired differences with an interval that includes zero are not evidence of a difference. Tied success is never an improvement. Validation loss on this task is not a proxy for success.
10. In a disagreement, engage with the implementer's specific argument: accept it, or name the number or rule that defeats it. Never restate a position without new reasoning, and never choose a middle option to end the disagreement.
11. Be specific and short. A hypothesis is one sentence that names a mechanism, not a wish.

An approved idea has been run. Judge, from the numbers below and nothing else, whether its prediction held.

{
  "id": "R-109",
  "title": "2. P2: Inherited structural evolution versus continued fixed fitting",
  "hypothesis": "LLM-selected state-feature connections exploit the inherited controller's failure statistics to produce larger sustained-success gains than grammar edits or continued fitting of the fixed structure.",
  "prediction": {
    "metric": "paired_success_difference",
    "direction": "increase",
    "threshold": 0.05,
    "against": "Grammar-based structural evolution with identical ARS and evaluation allocation",
    "rationale": "P2 is now eligible because D-075 confirmed a useful inner learner; neither earlier cold generation nor P1 tested inherited structural evolution. Use three independent search blocks, each starting from the hashed config/pen_spin/r106_success_ars_finalist/finalist.json. Compare fixed, grammar and LLM arms with K=2 candidates, U=3 updates and R=2 rounds. Grammar and LLM candidates inherit the current parent and each receive three exact-success ARS updates. The fixed arm instead follows one six-update continuation per round and submits its update-three and update-six snapshots as its two candidates, giving the unconverged fixed structure a strong, budget-matched control. Every arm receives 12 updates per block, identical training transitions and candidate-evaluation allocation. Preserve R-106's four directions, shared 512 placements per signed candidate, nu=0.02, alpha=0.01 and bounds. Implement a term-list interface around the existing features, residual and ARS, rather than a new learner. Freeze a common grammar of zero-initialized additive feature-to-joint/group blocks using clipped, normalized available observation primitives, products and bounded gates; no new memory in this pilot. Allow at most eight added coefficients per edit, 48 coefficients total, expression depth three and 256 total expression nodes; retain the existing 0.10 coefficient and residual bounds. Preserve old coefficients bit for bit, verify behavioral inheritance on identical observations and verify that signed coefficient perturbations activate new contributions. Grammar samples edits from this declared language; the LLM selects edits from the same language using only the current structure, coefficients and training/selection statistics. No free code. After each round, evaluate both candidates and the parent on 1,536 disjoint selection placements, arranged as three 512-case manifests in a fixed four-slot layout with a duplicate parent diagnostic. Rotate slots by a frozen schedule. Require the strict paired-success and drop gates against the parent, with Holm correction over the two candidate comparisons; otherwise retain the parent. All arms receive identical selection access. Freeze each block's three finalists before confirmation. Evaluate all three plus R-106 and D-072 on twelve fresh 128-case manifests per block, using one whole manifest per fresh process. The resulting 1,536 pairs per block provide at least approximately 80% unadjusted case-level power for a five-point primary contrast under discordance <=0.41. Analyze equal-weight block differences with a three-block t interval, alongside case-paired and manifest-level uncertainty; this is an algorithm pilot, not 4,608 independent search replicates. Prospectively size any stronger study from between-block variance rather than extending these confirmations. Also report grammar versus fixed, LLM versus fixed and both frozen-reference contrasts; preserve strict success/drop qualification and leave the saved incumbent unchanged. Reserve exactly 24 controller-call slots: 12 generation calls and at most one linked correction for each, with no other generation or retry calls. Use gpt-6.1-sol, high reasoning, temperature 1 and existing llm_pool with 16 workers. Invalid edits after correction become inherited no-op candidates with the full training/evaluation allocation. Run the driver in .venv-metaworld and launch every Isaac child through protocols.isaac_shell. Estimated simulator starts are 885,600 training, 221,184 selection, 46,080 confirmation and 4,096 smoke; ceiling 1,300,000. Atomically reserve 58 distinct live-ledger seeds before execution: one smoke, three training, eighteen selection and thirty-six confirmation manifests; the empty seed array is pending this allocation, not zero consumption. Implement the registry handler, interface and necessary tests before launch; reuse the existing scripts/configs and established evaluator. Record the full shared result contract, including per-block contrasts, complexity, inherited hashes and calls/tokens by role. Run only one protocol at a time and follow existing escalation/exhaustion and decision-recording workflows.\n\nFROZEN REVISION (triage round 2, agreed; supersedes the text above where they differ; nothing is simulated or generated before approval).\n\nSCHEDULE. Three independent blocks, each from the hashed R-106 finalist (config/pen_spin/r106_success_ars_finalist/finalist.json). K = 2 candidates, U = 6 exact-success ARS updates per candidate, R = 2 rounds. Structural arms (grammar, llm): each round, two candidate structures inherit the arm's current parent (its term list and coefficients, bit for bit) and each receives six updates. Fixed arm: one twelve-update continuation of the parent's structure per round, its snapshots after 6 and 12 updates being its two candidates. Every arm therefore spends 12 updates per round and 24 per block. ARS as R-106: 4 antithetic directions all used, nu 0.02, alpha 0.01, coefficient bound 0.10, residual cap 0.10, each signed candidate on the same 512 placements (two 2,048-environment rollouts per update), return = sustained-success fraction. Update u (0..11) of round r in block b uses cases.placements(training_seed_b, 12288)[512(12r+u) : 512(12r+u+1)] in every arm and for every candidate, and directions from default_rng(training_seed_b + 2000 + 100(12r+u) + candidate index); training seeds 4835, 4836, 4837. Placements are checked disjoint from every committed pen-spin manifest and from each other.\n\nTHE ACTOR AS A TERM LIST. residual_j = clip(sum over terms of coef[term, slot(j)] * E_term,j(observation), -0.10, +0.10); action = clamp(reference + residual, -1, 1). The inherited structure is three terms and 32 coefficients: [spin_deficit on target 'joints' (20)], [vel on 'groups' (6)], [posture on 'groups' (6)]; with those it must reproduce the R-106 finalist's actions bit for bit (smoke gate and unit test). No new memory state; the only state is the reference's velocity filter.\n\nEDIT LANGUAGE (shared by the grammar and LLM arms; one edit = ADD ONE TERM, zero-initialised). A term is {\"expr\": E, \"target\": T}.\nTargets (one coefficient per slot; at most 8 new coefficients per edit): 'groups' (6 slots: wrist, FF, MF, RF, LF, TH; applies to all 20 joints), 'chain:FF' (FFJ3, FFJ2, FFJ1), 'chain:MF' (3), 'chain:RF' (3), 'chain:LF' (LFJ4, LFJ3, LFJ2, LFJ1), 'chain:TH' (THJ4..THJ0, 5), 'wrist' (WRJ1, WRJ0). 'joints' (20) exists only for the inherited term.\nPrimitives, all from the 157-d observation and the reference action, each clipped as stated:\n  scalar in [0,1]: spin_deficit = clip((7 - |w|)/7, 0, 1); spin_level = clip(|w|/7, 0, 1); centre_dist = clip(|obj_pos - in_hand_pos|/0.08, 0, 1); transverse = clip(|transverse angular velocity|/7, 0, 1); tilt_up = |a_z| (a = pen long axis, world frame);\n  scalar in [-1,1]: centre_x, centre_y, centre_z = clip((obj_pos - in_hand_pos)_k/0.08, -1, 1); yaw_cos2 = a_x^2 - a_y^2; yaw_sin2 = 2 a_x a_y; phase_sin, phase_cos = sine and cosine of the pen's roll angle from the swing-twist decomposition about its local x (2 t_w t_x, t_w^2 - t_x^2), as the incumbent computes it; (w = signed axial rate in rad/s, angular velocities de-scaled by 1/0.2);\n  per finger, broadcast to that finger's chain joints and 0 on the wrist: tip_dist = clip(distance from the fingertip to the pen's 0.15 m axis segment / 0.06, 0, 1) in [0,1]; tip_axial_abs = clip(|fingertip coordinate along the pen axis|/0.07, 0, 1) in [0,1];\n  per joint (20): vel = clip(v_f/(3 rms_v), -1, 1) (the reference's filtered velocity, R-103 normalisation); posture = clip((reference_action - q)/(3 rms_e), -1, 1); ref = reference action in [-1,1]; pos = normalised joint position in [-1,1].\nOperators: [\"mul\", A, B] (elementwise product, broadcasting scalar/finger/joint); [\"gate\", A, c, \"above\"|\"below\"] = clip((A - c)/0.25, 0, 1) or clip((c - A)/0.25, 0, 1), A a [0,1]-valued expression, c in {0.25, 0.5, 0.75}; [\"comp\", A] = 1 - A for a [0,1]-valued A; [\"abs\", A] for a [-1,1]-valued A. Depth (a primitive is 1, an operator adds 1) at most 3; at most 7 nodes per expression; at most 48 coefficients and 256 expression nodes in a structure. Canonical form: JSON with mul arguments sorted by their serialisation; a term whose canonical (expr, target) already exists in the structure, or that was already tried in the block, is invalid; an expression must not be constant and must be nonzero on at least 5% of the block's stored observation sample (8,192 observation rows with their reference actions and filter values, saved from the parent's selection rollouts of that block), which is the activation check for new coefficients.\nGrammar arm sampling (default_rng(training_seed_b + 9000 + 10 r + k), resampled until valid): target 'groups' 0.4, a chain 0.5 (uniform over five), 'wrist' 0.1; depth 1 / 2 / 3 with probability 0.3 / 0.4 / 0.3; primitives uniform over those type-valid at the position; operator uniform over the type-valid ones.\nLLM arm: one generation call per candidate slot (3 blocks x 2 rounds x 2 slots = 12 calls) plus at most one linked correction each (24 controller-generation calls at most; gpt-6.1-sol, reasoning_effort high, temperature 1; llm_pool across blocks, slot 1 after slot 0 so it can see slot 0's edit). The reply is strict JSON {\"expr\": ..., \"target\": ..., \"rationale\": ...} in this language, validated by the same validator as grammar samples before any simulation; an edit still invalid after its correction becomes an inherited no-op candidate that receives its full six updates. The prompt contains only: the language above; the arm's current term list with coefficients; the parent's statistics on the round's selection placements (success, drops / slow spin / off-centre counts, mean |axial rate|, per-joint mean executed residual and saturation fraction, per-term mean |contribution|); the edits already tried in this block with their selection outcomes. Nothing from confirmation, nothing from other arms or blocks.\n\nSELECTION (in-process, shared placements; not the fresh-process evaluator). After a round's training, one process per (block, arm, round) runs three 2,048-environment batches; each batch holds four slots on the same 512 placements: parent, candidate 1, candidate 2, parent again (duplicate diagnostic), slot order rotated by one per batch. Selection seeds 4838-4855, one per (block, round, batch), shared by the three arms. A candidate replaces the parent only if, over the 1,536 placements, its paired sustained-success difference against the parent is positive with a Holm-adjusted (two candidates) two-sided paired t-test p < 0.05 and the one-sided 95% upper bound of its paired drop-rate difference is <= 0.05; if both pass, the larger mean difference wins; otherwise the parent is kept. The parent-vs-duplicate discordance and difference are reported. The block's finalist per arm is its parent after round 2, hashed in finalists.json before any confirmation case.\n\nCONFIRMATION. Twelve fresh 128-case manifests per block (seeds 4856-4891; config/manifests/pen_spin_stage3_structure_confirm_s<seed>.yaml), one whole manifest per fresh Isaac process: the D-072 reference, the R-106 finalist, and the block's fixed, grammar and llm finalists (a finalist identical to an already evaluated one reuses its cell). Per block 1,536 pairs per contrast. Primary: llm minus grammar, the equal-weight mean of the three block differences with its three-block t interval (2 degrees of freedom) governing the algorithm-level conclusion; case-paired pooled and manifest-clustered intervals reported beside it. Also grammar minus fixed, llm minus fixed, each arm minus the R-106 finalist and minus D-072 (strict paired rule and drop bound for usefulness). If neither structural arm beats the fixed arm, no structural-evolution contribution is claimed.\n\nSMOKE (seed 4834, one process, stops the study on failure): the term-list actor with the inherited structure equals the R-106 finalist controller bit for bit over a rollout; a structure with one added zero-coefficient term equals it bit for bit; a nonzero new coefficient changes the action; the scorer is live; A/A slots; throughput.\n\nBUDGET. Simulator starts: training 3 blocks x 3 arms x 24 updates x about 8,200 = 1,771,200; selection 3 x 3 x 2 x 3 batches x about 4,100 = 221,400; confirmation 3 x 12 x 5 x 128 cases charged at 2 = 46,080; smoke about 8,200: about 2.05 M; hard ceiling 2,300,000, enforced before every rollout; a started child is never relaunched from its seed. Wall time about 4.5 to 5 h (training 144 min, selection 30 min, confirmation 75 min, generation 30 min). Venue: the driver runs in .venv-metaworld (openai) and launches every Isaac child through protocols.isaac_shell. Three blocks: an algorithm pilot.\n\nROUND-3 CORRECTIONS (agreed; these override the frozen revision above where they differ).\n(a) Information timeline. Edit generation (grammar validity/activation check and the LLM prompt) never sees the selection rollouts that will gate its own candidates. Round 1: the smoke (seed 4834) runs the R-106 finalist on its own 512 placements and saves an 8,192-row observation sample (with reference actions and filter values) and the parent summaries (success, drop / slow-spin / off-centre counts, mean |axial rate|, per-joint executed residual and saturation, per-term mean |contribution|); every block and arm uses that same shared initialisation information in round 1. Round 2: only the retained parent's sample and statistics saved from round 1's selection rollouts (a sample is saved for every selection slot so the retained one is available without another rollout), plus the block's tried edits and their round-1 selection outcomes. A round's selection placements are revealed only after both of its candidates are trained and frozen (hashed in candidates_b<block>_<arm>_r<round>.json).\n(b) Training allocation. Global update index u in 0..11 per round. Structural candidate k in {0, 1}, local update i in 0..5, uses u = 6k + i (candidate 0: u 0-5, candidate 1: u 6-11); the fixed continuation uses u = 0..11 in order, its snapshots after u = 5 and u = 11 being its candidates 0 and 1. Placements for (round r, u): cases.placements(training_seed_b, 12288)[512(12r+u) : 512(12r+u+1)]; directions from default_rng(training_seed_b + 2000 + 100(12r+u)), regenerated at the candidate's own dimension. No candidate receives more than six updates per round and no arm more than twelve.\n(c) Configuration and command. The frozen block is pen_spin_structure in config/pen_spin_plateau_repair.yaml; no new top-level config.\n(d) falsified_by is the across-block interval's upper bound below 0.05; an interval containing zero establishes no advantage even if it also refutes the five-point magnitude."
